section.content: The present application provides a lithium ion battery. The lithium ion battery comprises a positive plate containing a positive active material, a negative plate containing a negative active material and electrolyte. The positive active material includes an inner core and a coating layer. The coating layer is coated on the surface of the inner core and contains boron element. The electrolyte includes a lithium salt, a non-aqueous organic solvent, and an electrolyte additive. The electrolyte additive includes an organic titanium compound. The coating layer of the lithium ion battery anode active material contains boron, the electrolyte contains an organic titanium compound, and the lithium ion battery has good high-temperature cycle performance and high-temperature storage performance under the combined action of the boron and the organic titanium compound.

本申请提供一种锂离子电池。所述锂离子电池包括包含正极活性材料的正极片，包含负极活性材料的负极片以及电解液。所述正极活性材料包括内核以及包覆层。所述包覆层包覆在所述内核的表面且所述包覆层中含有硼元素。所述电解液包括锂盐、非水有机溶剂以及电解液添加剂。所述电解液添加剂包括有机钛化合物。本申请的锂离子电池正极活性材料的包覆层中含有硼元素，且电解液中含有有机钛化合物，在两者的共同作用下锂离子电池具有较好的高温循环性能和高温存储性能。

Lithium ion batteryTechnical Field

The application relates to the field of batteries, in particular to a lithium ion battery.

Background

In recent years, lithium ion batteries have shown good application prospects in the fields of EVs, HEVs, energy storage devices, and the like, and have become a favorite in the fields. With the expansion of market demand of electronic products and the development of power and energy storage devices, the demand of people for energy density of lithium ion batteries is also increasing, and therefore, the development of lithium ion batteries with high energy density is urgent.

The development of a lithium ion battery positive active material with higher voltage or higher specific discharge capacity is a hot spot of research in recent years. However, when the voltage of the lithium ion battery is further increased or the specific discharge capacity is further increased, the stability of the positive active material itself becomes a very critical problem, and the side reaction between the positive active material and the electrolyte is further aggravated, and the electrochemical performance of the lithium ion battery is seriously deteriorated. In order to improve the electrochemical performance of a lithium ion battery under high voltage or high specific discharge capacity, more and more researchers are dedicated to modification research on a positive electrode active material, and the positive electrode active material used by the current power lithium ion battery mainly comprises lithium iron phosphate and ternary materials (NCM/NCA). Ternary lithium Nickel Cobalt Manganese (NCM) materials have received extensive attention from researchers due to their high capacity (up to 250mAh/g, 91% of theoretical capacity), good safety, low cost, and the like. However, for the power lithium ion battery, the lithium ion battery does not swell under high-temperature storage, has a long cycle service life as a key index, and the bottleneck that the ternary lithium Nickel Cobalt Manganese (NCM) material cannot give consideration to both high-temperature storage performance and cycle performance and limits the application of the ternary lithium Nickel Cobalt Manganese (NCM) material in the field of the power lithium ion battery. At present, the modification means of the ternary lithium-nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) material mainly comprises two means of bulk phase doping and surface coating, including the selection of some transition metal oxides or non-transition metal oxides to dope the positive active material, the coating of a layer of inert metal oxide on the surface of the positive active material and the like. However, when the precursor of the positive electrode active material is coated, the active site is not completely coated, and the rapid capacity decay of the positive electrode active material still cannot be prevented.

Therefore, it is highly desirable to provide a technical means to stabilize the positive active material during long-term cycling, so as to improve the performance of lithium ion batteries, such as high-temperature storage and cycle life.

Disclosure of Invention

In view of the problems in the background art, an object of the present invention is to provide a lithium ion battery, in which a coating layer of a positive electrode active material of the lithium ion battery contains boron, and an electrolyte contains an organic titanium compound, and the lithium ion battery has good high-temperature cycle performance and high-temperature storage performance under the combined action of the boron and the organic titanium compound.

In order to achieve the above object, the present application provides a lithium ion battery comprising a positive electrode sheet comprising a positive electrode active material, and a negative electrode sheet comprising a negative electrodeA negative electrode sheet of active material, and an electrolyte. The positive active material includes an inner core and a coating layer. The coating layer is coated on the surface of the inner core and contains boron element. The electrolyte includes a lithium salt, a non-aqueous organic solvent, and an electrolyte additive. The electrolyte additive comprises an organic titanium compound, wherein the organic titanium compound is selected from one or more of compounds shown in formula 1, formula 2, formula 3, formula 4 and formula 5; wherein R is1、R2、R3、R4、R5、R6、R7、R11、R12、R13、R14Each independently selected from substituted or unsubstituted C1-C12 alkyl, substituted or unsubstituted C1-C12 hydroxyalkyl, substituted or unsubstituted C2-C12 alkenyl, substituted or unsubstituted C2-C12 alkynyl, substituted or unsubstituted C1-C12 sulfonyl and metal ion, R8、R9、R10Each independently selected from one of substituted or unsubstituted C1-C12 alkyl, substituted or unsubstituted C2-C12 alkenyl, substituted or unsubstituted C2-C12 alkynyl and halogen, R21、R22、R23、R24、R25、R26、R27、R28Each independently selected from one of substituted or unsubstituted C1-C6 alkyl and substituted or unsubstituted C1-C6 sulfonyl.

Compared with the prior art, the beneficial effects of this application do:

the coating layer of the lithium ion battery anode active material contains boron, the electrolyte contains an organic titanium compound, and the lithium ion battery has good high-temperature cycle performance and high-temperature storage performance under the combined action of the boron and the organic titanium compound.

Detailed Description

The lithium ion battery according to the present application is explained in detail below.

First, a lithium ion battery according to a first aspect of the present application is explained.

The lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application includes a positive electrode sheet containing a positive electrode active material, a negative electrode sheet containing a negative electrode active material, and an electrolyte. The positive active material includes an inner core and a coating layer. The coating layer is coated on the surface of the inner core and contains boron element. The electrolyte includes a lithium salt, a non-aqueous organic solvent, and an electrolyte additive. The electrolyte additive includes an organic titanium compound. The organic titanium compound is selected from one or more compounds shown in formula 1, formula 2, formula 3, formula 4 and formula 5. Wherein R is1、R2、R3、R4、R5、R6、R7、R11、R12、R13、R14Each independently selected from substituted or unsubstituted C1-C12 alkyl, substituted or unsubstituted C1-C12 hydroxyalkyl, substituted or unsubstituted C2-C12 alkenyl, substituted or unsubstituted C2-C12 alkynyl, substituted or unsubstituted C1-C12 sulfonyl and metal ion, R8、R9、R10Each independently selected from one of substituted or unsubstituted C1-C12 alkyl, substituted or unsubstituted C2-C12 alkenyl, substituted or unsubstituted C2-C12 alkynyl and halogen, R21、R22、R23、R24、R25、R26、R27、R28Each independently selected from one of substituted or unsubstituted C1-C6 alkyl and substituted or unsubstituted C1-C6 sulfonyl.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, in the positive active material, on one hand, boron in the positive active material coating layer has good lithium ion diffusion capability, which can reduce DCR of the lithium ion battery, improve power performance of the lithium ion battery, and at the same time, can improve the first efficiency of the positive active material, thereby improving capacity of the lithium ion battery, and improve electrochemical performance of the lithium ion battery to a certain extent, and on the other hand, boron in the coating layer can also interact with transition metals (such as nickel, cobalt, manganese, and the like) in the positive active material core through electron complexation, so as to stabilize the crystal structure of the positive active material, reduce dissolution of the transition metals, and further improve power performance, high-temperature cycle performance, and high-temperature storage performance of the lithium ion battery; for the electrolyte, in the structure of the added electrolyte additive organic titanium compound, oxygen or nitrogen which is rich in electrons is connected with titanium, when the voltage is higher (more than 3.8V), electrochemical oxidation is easy to occur on the surface of the anode, uniform electrochemical deposition is performed on the surface of the anode, a titanium-containing film layer is formed and uniformly covers active sites of the anode active material, the corrosion of the electrolyte to the anode active material, particularly the corrosion to a coating layer, the dissolution of transition metal in the anode active material is further slowed down, the collapse of a crystal structure of the anode active material is prevented, and the purpose of further improving the electrochemical performance of the lithium ion battery is achieved. Therefore, the lithium ion battery of the application shows better high-temperature cycle performance and high-temperature storage performance under the combined action of the positive active material with the boron-containing element coating layer and the electrolyte containing the organic titanium compound.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the substituent may be selected from one or more of a halogen atom and an oxygen atom.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the core is selected from lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO)4) One or more of lithium cobalt oxide, lithium nickel oxide, lithium manganese oxide, lithium nickel cobalt aluminum oxide, and compounds obtained by adding other transition metals or non-transition metals to the above oxides; preferably, the core is selected from lithium cobaltate (LiCoO)2) Lithium manganate (LiMn)2O4) Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO)4) One or more of nickel-cobalt-manganese metal oxide (NCM); further, the method can be used for preparing a novel materialPreferably, the core is selected from the group consisting of LiNi1/3Co1/3Mn1/3O2、LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2、LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2、LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2One or more of them.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the core of the positive active material is divided into a large particle core and a small particle core, wherein the particle size D50 of the large particle core is 10 μm to 14 μm, the particle size D50 of the small particle core is 3 μm to 6 μm, and the large particle core and the small particle core are used in combination to increase the compaction density of the positive active material and increase the infiltration capacity of the electrolyte on the positive electrode plate due to capillary action.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, in the core of the positive electrode active material, the weight ratio of the large-particle core to the small-particle core is (5-9): (1-5), and in this range, the large-particle core and the small-particle core cooperate to further improve the compaction density of the positive electrode active material, thereby improving the energy density of the lithium ion battery.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the nickel content of the large particle cores is greater than or equal to the nickel content of the small particle cores, and since the total specific surface area of the small particle cores in the positive electrode active material is greater than the total specific surface area of the large particle cores, by controlling the nickel content of the large particle cores to be greater than or equal to the nickel content of the small particle cores, the probability of contact between the electrolyte and the nickel in the positive electrode active material can be reduced, so that side reactions between the electrolyte and the positive electrode active material are reduced, the DCR of the lithium ion battery is reduced, and the power characteristics of the lithium ion battery are improved.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the coating layer is selected from B2O3B compared to other B-containing materials2O3Higher diffusion capacity to lithium ion, DCR and work to lithium ion batteryThe improvement of the rate performance is more advantageous.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present invention, the content of the coating layer is 0.01% to 0.2% of the total weight of the positive electrode active material, and an excessively large content of the coating layer may cause deterioration of processability of the positive electrode active material and high-temperature storage performance of the lithium ion battery, and an excessively small content of the coating layer may not achieve the effect of improving the performance of the lithium ion battery, and preferably, the content of the coating layer is 0.02% to 0.1% of the total weight of the positive electrode active material.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the organic titanium compound is selected from one or more of tetrabutyl titanate, tetraethyl titanate, tetrapropyl titanate, diisopropyl di (acetylacetonate) titanate, tetraisopropyl titanate, tert-butoxytitanium, butylisopropyl titanate, titanium 2-methylpropanoate, tetrakis (3-hydroxypropanoxy) titanate, bis (2, 4-pentanedionato) titanium (IV) oxide, tetrakis (2, 4-pentanedionato) titanium (IV), bis (trifluoromethanesulfonic) titanocene, diisopropoxytitanium dichloride, diethoxytitanium dichloride, iodotriisopropyltitanate, and tetrakis (dimethylamino) titanium (IV), wherein the molecular formulae of each are as follows.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the content of the organic titanium compound is 0.001% to 0.5% of the total weight of the electrolyte, and if the added amount is too small, the organic titanium compound is not sufficient for effective electrochemical deposition under high voltage, and if the added amount is too large, the problem of high-temperature storage and gas expansion of the lithium ion battery may occur due to the difficulty in dissolving the organic titanium compound. Preferably, the content of the organic titanium compound is 0.001-0.1% of the total weight of the electrolyte.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the kind of the non-aqueous organic solvent is not particularly limited as long as it is satisfied that it does not contain active hydrogen and is polar. Specifically, the non-aqueous organic solvent may be one or more selected from ethylene carbonate, propylene carbonate, dimethyl carbonate, ethyl methyl carbonate, diethyl carbonate, methyl propyl carbonate, delta-valerolactone, methyl formate, ethyl formate, methyl acetate, ethyl acetate, propyl acetate, ethyl propionate, methyl butyrate, butyl formate, propyl propionate, ethyl butyrate, butyl acetate, methyl valerate, pentyl formate, propylene sulfate, ethyl methyl sulfate, tetrahydrofuran, 1, 3-dioxolane, 1, 3-dioxane, dimethoxymethane, diethoxymethane, 1, 2-dimethoxyethane, and 1, 2-diethoxyethane. The nonaqueous organic solvent used in the present application may be used alone or in combination of two or more kinds depending on the use. From a practical and commercial point of view, various carbonates and carboxylates are the most preferred non-aqueous organic solvents.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the type of the lithium salt is not particularly limited, and the lithium salt may be an organic lithium salt, and may also be an inorganic lithium salt, and specifically, the lithium salt may contain one or more of fluorine element, boron element, and phosphorus element. Preferably, the lithium salt is selected from lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF)6) Lithium tetrafluoroborate (LiBF)4) Lithium perchlorate (LiClO)4) Lithium hexafluoroarsenate (LiAsF)6) Lithium tetrafluoro oxalate phosphate (litfo), LiN (SO)2RF)2、LiN(SO2F)(SO2RF) Lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonylimide) LiN (CF)3SO2)2(abbreviated as LiTFSI), lithium bis (fluorosulfonyl) imide Li (N (SO)2F)2) (abbreviated as LiFSI) and lithium LiB (C) bis (oxalato-borate2O4)2(abbreviated as LiBOB) and lithium difluorooxalato borate LiBF2(C2O4) (abbreviated as LiDFOB), wherein, the substituent RF＝–CnF2n+1N is 1 to 10Is an integer of (1). Further preferably, the lithium salt is selected from LiPF6、LiN(SO2RF)2One or two of them.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the concentration of the lithium salt in the electrolyte is 0.5M to 2M (M ═ mol L)-1)。

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the negative active material is selected from one or more of graphite, a silicon-based material, and a tin-based material.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the positive electrode tab and the negative electrode tab further include a conductive agent and a binder, and the types of the conductive agent and the binder are not limited and can be selected according to actual needs.

In the lithium ion battery according to the first aspect of the present application, the lithium ion battery further includes an isolation film, the type of the isolation film is not limited, and may be selected according to actual requirements, specifically, the isolation film may be selected from one or more of a polyethylene isolation film, a polypropylene isolation film, and a polyvinylidene fluoride isolation film, and the isolation film may be in the form of a single-layer isolation film, or may be in the form of one or more of a multilayer composite isolation film formed from one or more of single-layer isolation films.

Next, a method for producing the positive electrode active material according to the second aspect of the present application will be described.

The method for producing a positive electrode active material according to the second aspect of the present application, for producing the positive electrode active material according to the first aspect of the present application, includes the steps of: firstly, weighing soluble salts of nickel, cobalt and manganese according to a ratio to prepare an aqueous solution, and preparing a precursor of an inner core by utilizing a coprecipitation technology; then mixing the obtained precursor with a lithium source, and sintering for the first time to obtain a kernel; and mixing the obtained core with a boron source, and sintering again to obtain the cathode active material.

In the preparation method of the cathode active material according to the second aspect of the present application, the soluble salt of nickel, cobalt, manganese is selected from one or more of hydrochloride, sulfate, nitrate of nickel, cobalt, manganese, and the concentration of the soluble salt is 4mol/L to 8 mol/L.

In the method for preparing a positive electrode active material according to the second aspect of the present application, the coprecipitate is selected from the group consisting of basic salts, and in particular, the coprecipitate is selected from the group consisting of potassium hydroxide, NH4HCO3、NaCO3One or more of them.

In the method for producing a positive electrode active material according to the second aspect of the present application, the lithium source is selected from Li2CO3、LiOH、LiNO3One or more of B and B2O3One or more of boric acid and ammonium pentaborate.

In the method for preparing a positive electrode active material according to the second aspect of the present application, the temperature rise rate during the first sintering is 2 ℃/min to 10 ℃/min, the temperature is raised to 800 ℃ to 960 ℃, the first sintering time is 10h to 20h, and the positive electrode active material is cooled to room temperature at a rate of 0.5 ℃/min to 2 ℃/min after the first sintering. The heating curve is adopted for primary sintering, so that the content of residual Li in a primary sintering product can be reduced, and the integrity of the crystal structure of the core of the positive active material is maintained. Preferably, the temperature rise rate is 4 ℃/min to 6 ℃/min, and more preferably, the temperature rise rate is 5 ℃/min. Preferably, the first sintering time is 12-18 h, and further preferably, the first sintering time is 16 h. Preferably, the cooling to room temperature is carried out at a rate of 0.8 ℃/min to 1.5 ℃/min after the first sintering, and more preferably at a rate of 1 ℃/min after the first sintering.

In the method for producing a positive electrode active material according to the second aspect of the present application, the temperature at which the secondary sintering is performed is 500 to 800 ℃, and the sintering time is 4 to 6 hours.

The present application is further illustrated below with reference to examples. It should be understood that these examples are for illustrative purposes only and are not intended to limit the scope of the present application.

In the following examples, reagents, materials and instruments used are commercially available unless otherwise specified.

Example 1

(1) Preparation of positive electrode active material

Firstly, mixing nickel sulfate, cobalt sulfate and manganese sulfate according to a molar ratio, preparing a solution with the total metal ion concentration of 5mol/L, and then respectively preparing a large-particle inner core precursor and a small-particle inner core precursor by controlling reaction time and pH value by using a hydroxide coprecipitation technology; then mixing the large-particle core precursor and the small-particle core precursor with a lithium source in proportion, sintering at 900 ℃ for 14h at the heating rate of 6 ℃/min, cooling to room temperature at the cooling rate of 1 ℃/min, and crushing to obtain the large-particle core and the small-particle core respectively, wherein the core is LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2D50 of the large particle core is 11 μm, D50 of the small particle core is 4 μm; then, ball milling and mixing the large particle inner core and the small particle inner core for 1h according to the weight ratio of 4:1, and adding a boron source B2O3Mixing and ball milling for 2h, loading the materials into a sagger, heating at a rate of 6 ℃/min, and sintering at 700 ℃ for 5h to obtain the cathode active material, wherein B2O3The content of the coating layer is 0.1% of the weight of the inner core.

(2) Preparation of positive plate

Mixing the obtained positive electrode active material, conductive agent acetylene black and binder polyvinylidene fluoride according to the weight ratio of 96:2:2, adding solvent N-methyl pyrrolidone, and fully stirring and mixing to form uniform positive electrode slurry; and coating the slurry on an aluminum foil of a positive current collector, and then drying and cold pressing to obtain the positive plate.

(3) Preparation of negative plate

Mixing graphite serving as a negative electrode active material, acetylene black serving as a conductive agent, styrene butadiene rubber serving as a binder and carboxymethylcellulose sodium serving as a thickening agent according to the weight ratio of 95:2:2:1, adding deionized water, and fully stirring and mixing to form uniform negative electrode slurry; and coating the slurry on a copper foil of a negative current collector, and then drying and cold pressing to obtain the negative plate.

(4) Preparation of the electrolyte

Mixing ethylene carbonate, diethyl carbonate and methyl ethyl carbonate according to the mass ratio of EC: DEC: EMC of 3:2:5 in a glove box filled with argon, then slowly adding lithium hexafluorophosphate with the concentration of 1.0mol/L into the mixed solution, finally adding an electrolyte additive, and uniformly stirring to obtain the electrolyte, wherein the electrolyte additive is tetraethyl titanate, and the content of the tetraethyl titanate is 0.1% of the total weight of the electrolyte.

(5) Preparation of lithium ion battery

Stacking the positive plate, the isolating film and the negative plate in sequence to enable the isolating film to be positioned between the positive plate and the negative plate to play an isolating role, and then winding to obtain a bare cell; placing the naked electric core in an outer packaging foil, injecting the prepared electrolyte into the dried electric core, and then carrying out the processes of vacuum packaging, standing, formation, shaping and the like to obtain the lithium ion battery.

(1) High temperature cycle performance testing of lithium ion batteries

Charging the lithium ion battery at a constant current of 1C to a voltage of 4.3V at 45 ℃, then charging at a constant voltage of 4.3V to a current of 0.05C, then discharging at a constant current of 1C until the final voltage is 2.8V, which is a charge-discharge cycle, taking the discharge capacity of the first cycle as 100%, then performing charge and discharge cycles, recording the discharge capacity of the lithium ion battery after 200 cycles, and calculating the capacity retention rate of the lithium ion battery after 200 cycles.

The capacity retention (%) after 200 cycles of the lithium ion battery was × 100% of the discharge capacity at 200 th cycle/the discharge capacity at the first cycle.

(2) High temperature storage performance testing of lithium ion batteries

Charging the lithium ion battery at a constant current of 1C to a voltage of 4.3V at 25 ℃, then charging at a constant voltage of 4.3V to a current of 0.05C, and then discharging at a constant current of 1C until the final voltage is 2.8V, wherein the first discharge capacity of the lithium ion battery is marked as C1Then fully charging the battery to 4.3V at 1C, charging the battery to 0.05C at constant voltage, then storing the fully charged lithium ion battery in a thermostat at 60 ℃ for 90 days, taking out the lithium ion battery every 30 days for testing, taking out the lithium ion battery after the 90-day storage is finished, discharging the lithium ion battery to 2.8V, charging the lithium ion battery to 4.3V at a constant current of 1C, then charging the lithium ion battery to 0.05C at a constant voltage of 4.3V, then discharging the lithium ion battery at a constant current of 1C until the final voltage is 2.8V, and recording the discharge capacity C of the lithium ion batteryn。

As can be seen from tables 1 and 2, in examples 1 to 8 and comparative example 1, the lithium ion battery containing the organic titanium compound as the electrolyte additive in the electrolyte has a high-temperature cycle capacity retention rate and a high-temperature storage capacity retention rate, and the organic titanium compounds with different structures can make the lithium ion battery have a high-temperature cycle capacity retention rate and a high-temperature storage capacity retention rate, which indicates that the organic titanium compound can effectively perform electrochemical deposition on the surface of the positive electrode during the cycle of the lithium ion battery, so that the lithium ion battery has excellent cycle performance and storage performance at high temperature. Even if the amount of the organic titanium compound is only 0.001% (example 5), the capacity retention of the lithium ion battery after 200 cycles can be improved by about 8% compared with comparative example 1 without the electrolyte additive organic titanium compound, so that it can be presumed that the organic titanium compound can effectively generate electrochemical deposition on the surface of the positive electrode and has a very obvious effect on passivating the surface of the positive electrode, the concentration of the organic titanium compound in the electrolyte is increased, the high-temperature cycle performance and the high-temperature storage performance of the lithium ion battery can be further improved, and the improvement on the cycle performance of the lithium ion battery is not significant after the content of the organic titanium compound in the electrolyte is increased to 0.2%.

In examples 1, 9-11 and comparative examples 8-9, B is absent2O3The positive active material of the coating layer has no stabilizing effect of boron on the core, so that the positive active material cannot resist the corrosion of the electrolyte, and the transition metal of the core can be dissolved out, so that the high-temperature circulation capacity retention rate and the high-temperature storage capacity retention rate of the lithium ion battery can be quickly attenuated. If B is2O3The coating layer is too thick, and at this time, although the reaction between the electrolyte and the positive electrode active material can be prevented, since the impedance is too high, more and more lithium ions cannot be smoothly extracted and inserted, and thus the high-temperature cycle capacity retention rate and the high-temperature storage capacity retention rate of the lithium ion battery are greatly reduced.

In examples 12 to 16 and comparative examples 3 to 7, when the organic titanium compound was used in combination with FEC, VC, VEC, PS, and DTD, the cycle performance and storage performance of the lithium ion battery were further improved since the FEC, VC, VEC, PS, and DTD formed a passivation film on the negative electrode, which could prevent damage to the negative electrode due to the byproduct of the reaction of the organic titanium compound, while the high temperature cycle performance and high temperature storage performance of the lithium ion battery using only FEC, VC, VEC, PS, and DTD as the electrolyte additive were not improved.

In conclusion, the coating layer of the positive active material of the lithium ion battery contains boron, the electrolyte contains the organic titanium compound, and the lithium ion battery has better high-temperature cycle performance and high-temperature storage performance under the combined action of the boron and the organic titanium compound.
